items.title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices rise from tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol and unsubsidised RON95 petrol will increase by 20 sen per litre each, while unsubsidised diesel will rise by 15 sen per litre from Sept 24 to 30. The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the new prices would be RM5.05 per litre for RON97, RM4.57 per litre for unsubsidised RON95 and RM5.42 per litre for unsubsidised diesel. It said continued supply constraints on refined petroleum products had kept market prices elevated.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH to announce candidates one to two weeks before nomination
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin. "This time, we are better prepared to name our candidates," he told reporters after visiting beneficiaries of the Ziarah Kasih programme at the Kuala Linggi state constituency. Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary's Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week.

items.title: Brazilian singer, 4 others killed in helicopter crash
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Five people, including Brazilian singer Rick Sollo of the sertanejo music duo Rick & Renner, were found dead Tuesday after their helicopter crashed in a mountainous area of southern Brazil's Santa Catarina state, the fire department said, Xinhua reported. Brazil's civil aviation agency said the aircraft, a Bell 430 manufactured in 2001, was authorised to operate. Rick & Renner is one of Brazil's most well-known sertanejo music duos with a career dating back to the 1980s.

items.title: Teacher-student scandal exposed after hotel visits, video recording
items.summary: SERDANG: A female teacher's alleged inappropriate relationship with her 17-year-old male student came to light after his family and school authorities discovered a video involving the two. The relationship is believed to have started last year, with the pair allegedly checking into hotels in Seri Kembangan several times and meeting at the teacher's home. The source said the teacher allegedly engaged in sexual acts with the student and recorded them on her mobile phone.

items.title: Agriculture Ministry denies mandatory 20pc padi deduction rate
items.summary: The ministry said deduction rates depended strictly on the physical condition and quality of the padi at the time of sale. "Padi delivered at optimum quality will attract significantly lower deduction rates in accordance with established standards. "To ensure transparency and prevent misconduct, the ministry, through the state-level Padi and Rice Regulatory Section, initiated nationwide special monitoring operations on padi grading on Sept 14," it said in a statement.

items.title: MNRB's FY26 final dividend at 15 sen per share
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MNRB Holdings Bhd has declared a final dividend of 15 sen per share for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with one-third of the payout eligible for reinvestment under its dividend reinvestment plan (DRP). Under the plan, shareholders may choose to receive the entire dividend in cash, reinvest the full eligible portion into new MNRB shares and receive the balance in cash, or reinvest part of the eligible portion and receive the remainder in cash. The authority for the company to issue new shares under the DRP was approved by shareholders at the company's annual general meeting on Sept 26, 2025.

items.title: Tourism Malaysia seeks bigger 2027 Budget allocation to hit 47mil arrivals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tourism Malaysia is seeking a higher allocation under Budget 2027 to help achieve its target of 47 million international tourist arrivals under the Visit Malaysia campaign, which has been extended until 2027. Its director-general, Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim, said the additional allocation was important to sustain Malaysia's promotion in international markets and ensure the country remained competitive in attracting tourists. He said the request also took into account the views of tourism industry players, who hoped allocations for the sector could be increased to strengthen efforts to promote Malaysia globally.

items.title: Aneka Jaringan bags RM26mil serviced apartment works
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aneka Jaringan Holdings Bhd's unit Aneka Jaringan Sdn Bhd (AJSB) has bagged a RM26.2 million contract for earthworks, piling and substructure works for a high-rise serviced apartment development in Jalan Yap Kwan Seng, Kuala Lumpur. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said AJSB received the letter of award from WDA Architects Sdn Bhd, acting on behalf of developer Exsim YKS 54 Sdn Bhd. The contract involves earthworks, piling and pile caps, retaining walls and sub-structure works for a 53-storey serviced apartment development.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 23, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Rosmah fights judgment Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor will resist enforcement of a RM67.5 million judgment over 43 missing pieces of jewellery. Anwar slams move Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised the move to remove Negri Sembilan Ruler Tuanku Muhriz as disrespectful and uncivilised. Teen assaulted mother A psychiatric report says a 15-year-old boy assaulted his mother 13 days before the fatal stabbing of a schoolmate last year.

items.title: Rimbunan Sawit takes RM10mil hit from blockade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rimbunan Sawit Bhd estimates a revenue shortfall of about RM10 million following a three-month disruption at its Ulu Teru Estate in Miri, caused by a blockade of the estate's main access route. The Sarawak-based plantation group said the blockade, which disrupted access since June 18, was lifted on Sept 15 with estate operations fully resuming on Sept 21. Ulu Teru Estate is operated by PJP Pelita Ulu Teru Plantation Sdn Bhd, which is 60 per cent-owned by Nescaya Palma Sdn Bhd.

items.title: RoS asks PN to explain why it should not be deregistered
items.summary: A source confirmed to Berita Harian that the notice had been sent to the PN chairman, secretary-general and all PN component parties yesterday. The New Straits Times have reached out to RoS. The RoS had previously confirmed receiving an official complaint from Bersatu on Aug 11 against PN.

items.title: Two schoolgirls injured after being hit by motorcycle in Permatang Pauh
items.summary: Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police had detected a 30-second video of the incident circulating on social media. "Preliminary investigations found that the two pupils were crossing the pedestrian crossing before being hit by a motorcycle ridden by an unidentified individual," he said. Nik Aminuddin said police were investigating to identify the motorcyclist and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

items.title: Three foreign students held over suspected murder in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH: Police have detained three foreign students over the suspected murder of a local man in Kampung Kuchai here on Sept 18. Ipoh police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the three suspects, aged between 17 and 20, were arrested at their apartment this morning. Najib said police subsequently arrested the three suspects as part of investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

items.title: UUCA replacement Bill expected to be tabled in December, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The first reading of the Bill to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) is expected to be tabled at the Dewan Rakyat sitting in December, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the ministry is working to complete a comprehensive series of engagements with stakeholders to ensure the Bill accounts for the entire national higher education ecosystem before it is tabled in Parliament. Meanwhile, turning to Budget 2027, Zambry expressed hope that the Higher Education Ministry would secure a larger allocation to support the Malaysian Higher Education Development Plan.

items.title: Two Mandiri-linked individuals remanded three days over money laundering probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two individuals linked to non-governmental organisation (NGO) Mandiri have been remanded for three days to assist investigations under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA). Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi and Dobby Chew, who is director of Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd, were detained by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department's Anti-Money Laundering Investigation Team (AMLA) yesterday. The arrests followed an investigation paper opened on Sept 10 concerning the receipt of funds suspected to be proceeds from unlawful activities between 2024 and 2026.

items.title: Auku replacement Bill expected to be tabled in December – Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The first reading of the Bill that will replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (Auku) is expected to be tabled at the Dewan Rakyat sitting in December, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the ministry was working to complete a comprehensive series of engagements with stakeholders to ensure the Bill took into account the entire national higher education ecosystem before it was tabled in parliament. "We understand that when drafting a new Act, we must take into account the entire ecosystem of the national higher education system," he said.

items.title: ADB raises Malaysia’s 2026, 2027 growth forecasts to 4.9pc, 4.7pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has raised its 2026 and 2027 economic growth forecasts for Malaysia to 4.9 per cent and 4.7 per cent, respectively. In its September 2026 report, ADB said Malaysia’s growth is expected to moderate slightly in the second half of 2026 (2H 2026) and in 2027. Domestic spending will likely remain resilient, but heightened downside pressures may limit labour and consumption growth, it said.

items.title: BN to decide on Melaka polls cooperation soon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will soon decide whether to cooperate with other political parties for the 16th Melaka state election. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said the decision would be made after discussions with its top leadership in Melaka. [[nid:1539542]] The dissolution paves the way for the 16th Melaka state election.

items.title: Melaka election postal voting applications open
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka election opened today. Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said all applications must be submitted online via the MySPR portal, with the closing date to be announced later. Khairul Shahril said Category 1A applications covered police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel.

items.title: Search for missing fireman in Nepal: Hani prays for closure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing after flash floods struck Nepal, said she has come to terms with whatever fate awaits her husband. Hani Othman said she and her family had resigned themselves to fate after 29 days of enduring a deeply trying period. "Whatever fate God has for my husband, whether he returns to our family or returns to his creator, my family and I accept it.

items.title: SPR: Postal voting applications for Melaka polls open today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 —Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka State Election open today. Khairul Shahril said applications under Category 1A cover police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel. Melaka State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum also submitted the dissolution notice to the EC yesterday.

items.title: Rehda asks for special Home Ownership Campaign targeted at unsold completed units for 2027 budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia has called on the government to introduce a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) next year to tackle the issue of existing unsold completed residential units. Rising infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory, and compliance costs cumulatively impact project viability and housing affordability. Rehda also called for affordability impact assessments for major new policies, regulations, standards and charges affecting residential development.

items.title: Dollar at 2-month highs as Fed outlook 'dominant'
items.summary: LONDON: The dollar rose to its strongest level in two months on Wednesday on prospects of interest rate hikes in the near term, although easing oil prices could alter the global inflation and monetary policy outlook. Sterling was down 0.3 per cent at US$1.3305. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six others, was 0.24 per cent higher at 100.79.

items.title: Wife questions husband's late-night outings, gets slapped, headbutted and choked
items.summary: Kangar police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the incident, which occurred around 9.30pm was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the 49-year-old victim and her 56-year-old husband, who works as a lorry driver. He said the woman had earlier confronted her husband and asked him not to leave the house at night as she suspected he wanted to meet another woman. "The victim, who tried to defend herself, scratched the suspect's shoulder.

items.title: Rising costs, end-financing pose as challenges to property development in 1H 2026 – Rehda survey
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian property developers continue to face considerable pressure from rising costs, financing constraints, and uncertainties in the wider economic environment, according to Rehda Malaysia president Datuk Zaini Yusoff. Cost pressures were widespread during the first half of 2026, with 81 per cent of survey respondents reporting an increase in the cost of doing business. Of those respondents, 35 per cent experienced cost increases of between three and six per cent.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, weakens versus US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against major currencies on Wednesday but weakened against the greenback as expectations of further interest rate hikes by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) continued to support the US dollar. "The ringgit actually started the day stronger, reaching RM4.0640 against the US dollar in the morning. As the US dollar remained firm, the ringgit weakened to around RM4.0780 in the afternoon.

items.title: ‘Decision has been made’: Anthony Loke firm on resignation, to hand in letter upon return from China
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he remains firm in his decision to resign as Transport Minister. The Seremban MP said he would hand in his resignation letter upon returning home from China. I will submit the resignation letter to the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) when I return home,” he told reporters briefly after arriving in Hangzhou today.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 23, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower, weighed down by profit-taking in selected heavyweight counters and weakness in petrochemical-related stocks as oil prices retreated. The benchmark index ended seven points lower at 1,676.43. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin retreated to RM348,956.

items.title: 'I follow Chief Secretary's directive, continue duties in Negri Sembilan as usual,' says Zafir
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said he would continue performing his duties as usual, in accordance with the directive issued by the Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. He said the Chief Secretary had instructed him to remain in his post and continue serving in Negri Sembilan. "Tan Sri asked me to continue performing my duties as usual.

items.title: Loke maintains decision to quit Cabinet
items.summary: HANGZHOU: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he is sticking to his decision to quit the Cabinet. Loke, who is Transport Minister, said he will submit his resignation letter once he returns to Malaysia from China. However, he said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain within the federal administration.

items.title: 2027 Budget : Construction, AI, infrastructure sectors to benefit – Moomoo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Oct 9, is expected to benefit the construction and building materials sectors, based on current market consensus of RM85 billion to RM90 billion in development expenditure, according to Moomoo. It said beyond traditional construction materials, grid and water infrastructure, renewable energy and energy storage could also benefit from development spending. Moomoo noted that current market consensus estimates put 2027 Budget's total expenditure at around RM438.9 billion, comprising approximately RM353.1 billion in operating expenditure and RM85.8 billion in development expenditure.

items.title: 13 areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 197
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thirteen areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with the Serian district police headquarters recording the highest reading at 197. Unhealthy readings were also recorded in Samalaju (164), Miri (161), Mukah (160), Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (155), Limbang (153) and Kapit (120). Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while nine recorded good readings.

items.title: No motion of no confidence submitted yet – Johari
items.summary: BANGI: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting. Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure. Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.

items.title: Technician gets RM20,000 bail over restaurant assault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A technician charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a businessman during an assault at a restaurant has been granted RM20,000 bail with one surety. High Court judge Nurulhuda Nur'aini Mohamad Nor allowed the bail application by Lai Kae Bin, 33. Firdaus said a review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that Lai's involvement in the incident was minor.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidates to be announced one to two weeks ahead of nomination, says PM’s pol-sec
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 23 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said Prime Minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin. He said the move would allow PH to make early preparations instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates. Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary’s Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week.

items.title: Police announce three‑stage road closures for Kuching Marathon from Sept 26 to 27
items.summary: These include the Jalan Pearl-Jalan Wawasan traffic lights towards Padang Merdeka, Lebuh Wayang-Jalan Wawasan, Jalan McDougall-Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg, and Susur Jalan Haji Taha. Also affected are the Jalan Ajibah Abol traffic lights, Jalan Muhibbah-Jalan Kulas junction, Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob-Jalan Merdeka junction, Jalan Kampung Lintang-Jalan Astana traffic lights, Mahkamah roundabout, Sesco roundabout, and Samariang roundabout. The closures will also cover the Jalan Sultan Tengah traffic lights near the fire station and Sego, Yayasan roundabout, Kesuma Resort roundabout, Stadium roundabout, Gersik roundabout, Merrican Salleh-Jalan Kwong Lee Bank traffic lights, Tanah Putih Clinic traffic lights, Jalan Sekama-Pending traffic lights, Sri Aman roundabout, and Jalan Gamelan-Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob junction.

items.title: Man dies in suspected electrocution in Lahad Datu
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Sept 23 — A man in his 30s died after he was believed to have been electrocuted at Kampung Puyut here today. The man, who had yet to be identified, was believed to have no identification document and was not recognised by local villagers, said Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid. He said the department received a distress call at 12.47pm and deployed 12 personnel to the scene, where the man was found electrocuted and was later confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel.

items.title: Bring umbrellas: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in KL and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states affected are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kedah, the areas expected to be affected are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak. The same warning has been issued for Kelantan, covering Jeli and Kuala Krai; Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu); and Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan).

items.title: Anwar: Negeri Sembilan MB and executive council’s bid to remove ruler was ‘rude and uncivilised’
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim criticised the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council for attempting to remove Yang di‑Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, calling the move rude and uncivilised. He said no state‑level authority has the mandate to question or alter the position of the Ruler, according to Berita Harian . Anwar said the crisis involving state administration and customary authority in Negeri Sembilan had become increasingly complex.

items.title: Anwar asks Loke to review decision to quit Cabinet after Najib’s conditional pardon
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Transport Minister Anthony Loke to rethink his plan to step down from the Cabinet following the Pardons Board’s decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon. In a New Straits Times report, Anwar said DAP should not give in to political pressure from groups seeking instability in the unity government. “Some people ask, why Anthony Loke?

items.title: Structural checks at Cheras apartment will take several days following landslide, says Selangor exco
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents evacuated from Block D of the Damai Perdana Apartments in Cheras may have to remain out of their homes for several days while authorities determine whether the building is structurally safe. Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Zone 6 councillor Tan Kah Hoe said multiple technical agencies were conducting assessments of the affected block, according to New Straits Times . Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras were ordered to evacuate their homes last night after a landslide occurred near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak.

items.title: Sabah man bites ex-girlfriend and threatens to kill her, gets RM5,800 fine
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A 35-year-old man was fined RM5,800 after pleading guilty to hurting his ex-girlfriend and threatening to kill her. Mohd Aideed Husein pleaded guilty before two Magistrates, Dzul Elmy Yunus and Marilyn Kelvin, to separate charges over the incident involving the 30-year-old woman on Sept 15. Before Dzul Elmy, he was fined RM1,800, in default six months’ jail, under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to the woman outside a shop at Lorong Suria Inanam 1.

items.title: Expedite court proceedings to settle Negeri Sembilan royal dispute, says ex-minister Syed Hamid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Court proceedings related to the Negeri Sembilan royal institution dispute should be expedited to provide a definitive resolution to the legal questions involved, former law minister Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar said. He said the dispute, which involves the adat (customary practices), state law and the Federal Constitution, should be resolved through the legal process rather than public debate or sentiment. Syed Hamid also urged all parties to refrain from making conflicting public statements, saying these could heighten public anxiety and make it more difficult to reach a reasonable and rational resolution.

items.title: TVET graduates may have jobs, but are they the right jobs? MEF asks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a broader assessment of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduate employability to better reflect their skills, career progression and contribution to the workforce. MEF senior adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the federation supported Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir’s call for the employability of Polytechnic and Community College (PolyCC) graduates to be assessed beyond headline employment percentages. He said the 2025 employability rates of 98.5 per cent for polytechnic graduates and 98.8 per cent for community college graduates were encouraging, but the quality and relevance of employment should also be considered in evaluating TVET outcomes.

items.title: Kota Bharu trader’s no-show lands him an arrest warrant over 42 cooking oil charges
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — The Sessions Court here today issued an arrest warrant for the owner of a subsidised cooking oil business after he failed to appear before the court to face charges involving the management of records and documents for the controlled item. Judge Nik Habri Muhamad issued the arrest warrant for Pui Tiong Lam, 61, for failing to appear in court for today’s prosecution proceedings without a valid reason. The court set Nov 5 for mention.

items.title: AG says Negeri Sembilan state secretary and legal adviser remain in office, must continue duties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Negeri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal must continue carrying out their duties because their suspension by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is invalid. Dusuki said, “The duties of Mohd Zafir as Negeri Sembilan state secretary and Muzalmah as state legal adviser must continue as usual, and they must also remain in Negeri Sembilan.” Dusuki said the situation in Negeri Sembilan mirrors the 2009 Perak crisis, when the state secretary and state legal adviser were also suspended.

items.title: Kelantan telecoms at risk of major outages as cable vandalism and theft soar, says says regional MCMC official
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — Vandalism and theft of telecommunications infrastructure in Kelantan have reached an alarming level and could disrupt communication coverage and the livelihoods of people if critical infrastructure is affected. Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Eastern Region Office senior director Mohd Fairus Muhamad said these incidents have also impacted the telecommunications industry, which bears millions of ringgit in losses for repair and restoration work. He said MCMC, together with enforcement authorities and industry players, is tightening coordination, including proposing a Telecommunications Infrastructure Vandalism Prevention Sub-Committee involving MCMC, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities, the Land and District Office and industry players.

items.title: Psychosis impaired teen’s understanding he was taking a life in Bandar Utama school murder, court says, rejecting months‑long planning claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The Shah Alam High Court rejected claims that the 16-year-old schoolgirl’s murder in Bandar Utama last year was planned for months, finding that the accused’s psychotic illness impaired his understanding of the act and that the alleged “plan” stemmed from his delusions. In her full written grounds, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said she could not accept that merely knowing he was pushing a knife into the deceased’s abdomen and that it would cause her to bleed was sufficient to establish that the accused understood the nature of the act. She added that an accused who has knowledge of the mechanics but not of the reality of what he is doing cannot be said to know the nature of the act.

items.title: Budget 2027 wishlist: Rehda wants wider housing loan access, special campaign for unsold units
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) Malaysia for Budget 2027. The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units. Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.

items.title: Who was he? A month on, mystery deepens over man found dead in KLIA aircraft landing gear
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 23 — The identity of a man whose body was found in an aircraft’s landing gear compartment at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 on Aug 27 remains unknown and the remains have yet to be claimed. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police had yet to receive any information that could establish the man’s identity. Asked how the man came to be inside the aircraft, Shazeli said the circumstances remained a mystery and were still under investigation.

items.title: Former Kelantan Kafa teacher gets RM2,000 fine for kicking Year Five pupil in face during class
items.summary: KUALA KRAI, Sept 23 — A former Religious and Fardu Ain Class (Kafa) teacher was fined RM2,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today for kicking a Year Five pupil in the face, causing injuries to his gums. Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid imposed the maximum fine, with a default of four months in jail, after Abdullah Mustakim, 33, pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to the pupil in a classroom at a school here at about 2.30 pm on Oct 23, 2024. The kick caused an injury to the pupil’s gums.

items.title: Anwar courts Chinese industry leaders with eye on investments in chips, AI and robotics
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — A roundtable discussion with industry leaders from 21 leading Chinese companies here focused on various high-impact sectors, including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics, as Malaysia explores high-value strategic investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The discussion also touched on the potential of electric vehicles (EVs), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology, healthcare, specialty chemicals and advanced manufacturing. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook also participated in the discussion.

items.title: Rosmah’s RM67.5m jewellery bill: No pause button, Court of Appeal rules
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has lost her latest bid to fully halt a RM67.5 million payment owed to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL over dozens of missing jewellery pieces. The Court of Appeal has dismissed her appeal against a High Court order for a conditional stay, meaning the sum must still be deposited into a stakeholder account within a month of the August 12 judgement, The Edge reported today. The dispute traces back to a June High Court ruling by Judicial Commissioner Datuk Quay Chew Soon, which held Rosmah liable for 43 pieces of jewellery that went missing after a 2018 police raid.

items.title: Zero motions, zero Bills: Dewan Rakyat Speaker still waiting on no-confidence bid, PM term-limit, and AG-PP split
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 23 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said he has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting. Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure. Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.

items.title: Three-day remand for two men as Sarawak police probe convenience store fire cases
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Two men aged 40 and 23 were remanded for three days by the Magistrates’ Court here today to assist investigations into a case of mischief by fire involving a convenience store along Jalan Green here. The court ordered both suspects to be remanded for three days from Sept 23 to Sept 26 to assist investigations under Section 436 of the Penal Code. Three suspects have been arrested and remanded to assist investigations into both incidents.

items.title: Haze eases in Lubok Antu, but Kanowit air remains ‘very unhealthy’ at midday
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Lubok Antu moved out of the very unhealthy category by noon today after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropped from 205 at 8am to 195. Most monitoring stations across Sarawak also remained in the unhealthy category at noon, with readings ranging from 105 to 195. Under the API classification, readings of 0–50 are considered good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy and 201–300 very unhealthy.

items.title: Teen accused in Bandar Utama school killing diagnosed with early-onset schizophrenia and viewed others as ‘non-player characters’
items.summary: In her full grounds of judgment, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said this was disclosed in a psychiatric report prepared by Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, the director and senior consultant forensic psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta. In disclosing his findings, Dr Ian highlighted the existence of a “ Death Note ” journal on the accused’s mobile phone, in which he repeatedly referred to the deceased while chronicling the disturbing and psychotic thoughts in his mind. Psychiatric report findings The psychiatric report also noted a strong family history of mental illness, including an institutionalised aunt, a mentally disordered paternal grand-uncle and two affected sons, as well as a family member treated for depression.

items.title: ‘Your country is proud of you’, Anwar tells 22 Malaysians competing at WorldSkills Shanghai
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hailed Malaysia’s 22 young competitors at the 48th WorldSkills Competition here as the country’s pride, stressing that skilled workers are indispensable to a modern, technology-driven economy. Touching on youth’s role in the economy, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said young skilled workers play a crucial role in keeping modern economies running, even as machinery and software become increasingly sophisticated. Anwar said young people would be drawn to technical and skilled professions if they could see clear prospects for career advancement and better livelihoods.

items.title: Overseas markets key to growing Malaysia’s oil and gas services sector in next three years, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The government expects the oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) sector to increase its output and revenue in the next two to three years through expansion into overseas markets, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. Speaking to reporters today, he said greater international market participation would strengthen the sector’s revenue streams while improving the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies against economic and industry shocks. Akmal Nasrullah said international diversification was important to strengthen the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies and reduce their reliance on the domestic market.

items.title: New Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route on the cards as China Eastern eyes more Sabah flights
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — China Eastern Airlines plans to increase its Shanghai-Kota Kinabalu services to double or even triple daily flights, while exploring a direct Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route. Also present were Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry Permanent Secretary Datuk Josie Lai and representatives from the Sabah Tourism Board. — Daily Express Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin (centre) receives a memento from China Eastern Airlines (Sales & Marketing) Senior Vice President Yang Chun Fei (left).
